subject: Re: AtlasVault — deal-driven GPU SKU rebalancing & escalator language
messages:
From: Eve Sanchez <eve@atlasvault.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Moreno <cto@atlasvault.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: GPU SKU flexibility for reserved commit (AtlasVault)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is aligned on Redwood's latency profile. Before we finalize the reserved commit, procurement asked whether we can carve in some SKU flexibility. Two specific asks: 

1) A 12-month window after go-live where AtlasVault may swap up to 30% of reserved vGPU SKUs between families (e.g., shift from A100 to A10x) without re-pricing.
2) A narrow escalator clause: if provided hardware-class market prices rise >25% vs baseline, AtlasVault accepts a capped pass-through (max +12% invoice impact) or an agreed discount step-down.

Can you outline how Redwood would operationalize a "reserve-sku swap window" and whether finance/legal would accept an escalator cap? I've attached our internal T&Cs and a short requirements sheet (attachment: atlas_requirements.pdf).

Best,
Eve
Procurement Lead, AtlasVault

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Eve Sanchez <eve@atlasvault.com>
Cc: Carlos Moreno <cto@atlasvault.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 18:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GPU SKU flexibility for reserved commit (AtlasVault)

Eve — thanks, this is very clear. Quick replies inline: 

> 12-month swap window where AtlasVault may swap up to 30% of reserved SKUs
We can offer a one-time "reserve-sku rebalance" during months 6-12 post-go-live. Operationally that is a scheduled migration window: we tag the reservation, perform capacity checks, and apply the SKU swap as a planned change to the Dedicated pool. It requires 14 days lead-time for capacity validation.

> Escalator clause if hardware-class prices rise >25%
We are open to an escalator, but finance needs a deterministic cap to model risk. Marcus (cc'd) — can you confirm what threshold the finance team would accept as a capped pass-through and what approvals are needed?

I'll pull together a short attachment that sketches the mechanics and a proposed clause.

Thanks — KP
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Eve Sanchez <eve@atlasvault.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: RE: GPU SKU flexibility for reserved commit (AtlasVault)

Eve / Kimberly —

I reviewed the proposal and ran a scenario table (attached spreadsheet: proposed_sku_rebalance.xlsx). High-level finance position:

- We can support a single reserve-sku rebalance (up to 30%) in months 6–12, provided AtlasVault agrees to a quarterly true-up and a 14-day capacity validation window. That mitigates short-term provisioning churn.
- For an escalator: if Redwood's weighted GPU input cost (market vendor index in our model) increases by more than 25% versus the baseline we used at contract signature, we will allow a pass-through up to +12% of the committed monthly spend. Any pass-through above +12% requires VP Finance + VP Sales sign-off (internal approval).
- Finance can approve list-price discounts up to 20% at deal-signing for committed tenor. Anything deeper must go to the Revenue Committee for a governance exception.

Operational note: to keep things auditable, we need two items in the contract: a calculation appendix that cites the market index we will use, and a short service change process describing how a SKU rebalance is requested and validated.

Attaching a draft clause for the escalator (draft_price_escalator.docx) and the scenario workbook.

If AtlasVault prefers a capped discount instead of pass-through, we can offer a stepped discount schedule tied to the index bands instead of a straight pass-through.

—Marcus
Director, Finance — Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Eve Sanchez <eve@atlasvault.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: GPU SKU flexibility for reserved commit (AtlasVault)

Eve — quick commercial proposal to keep the deal simple: 

Option A (preferred for predictability): 24-month reserved commitment, single 30% swap window at month 9, quarterly true-up, escalator with pass-through cap at +12% (per Marcus). Offer a 10% one-time commitment discount on committed units.

Option B (if AtlasVault wants lower price exposure): 12-month committed tenor, no swap window, 5% additional discount but escalator resets to allow pass-through up to +8% (smaller cap; finance ok with this model).

Operational asks for AtlasVault: confirm preferred tenor and whether you want pass-through or tiered discount. If you confirm by EOD Friday we can route for Revenue Committee pre-approval and lock the SKU swap window into SOW.

Thanks — Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Eve Sanchez <eve@atlasvault.com>, Carlos Moreno <cto@atlasvault.com>

Eve / Carlos — thanks for the clear asks and quick turnaround. Summary and next steps: 

1) We will propose Option A as the recommended path: 24-month commit, single 30% swap window at month 9, quarterly true-up, escalator with a +12% pass-through cap.
2) Marcus will include the market-index appendix and the short change process in the SOW.
3) Rishi will submit the commercial terms to Revenue Committee for a pre-approval (target decision by Tue next week).
4) Kimberly to schedule a 30-minute call with AtlasVault + Redwood Finance/Legal to walk the clause and the operational flow.

Attachments: proposed_sku_rebalance.xlsx (scenario workbook), draft_price_escalator.docx (clause language), atlasvault_security_brief.pdf (reference).

Can you confirm that the timing works for a July 7th 09:00 PT call? If so we will send a calendar invite and prepare the SOW draft.

Best,
